speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what additional noise abatement measures to counter low-flying aircraft noises coming from the nearby Seletar Airport can be put in place; (b) whether the height limit of the airspace over residential areas can be increased; and (c) whether a different flight path can be given to aircraft landing at the airport so that they will not fly over housing estates, especially in the middle of the night.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: CAAS has considered raising the height of such flight paths.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, this would compromise the safety of the aircraft because the aircraft will have to ascend or climb and descend at steeper angles.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Actually, it is not just sometimes, as the Minister mentioned.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On 3 January, there were three flights coming in ­—

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Yes, I would like to ask whether we can limit the time further, because if you mention 10.00 pm to 7.00 am, it is not true.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: There are flights that come in at 3.00 am, 4.00 am and 5.00 am.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: It is continuous – on 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 January.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And there are flights that come in after 10.00 pm.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, for those that are noisy, can we turn them away or not allow them to land at Seletar Airport at all and not come near Nee Soon South because they wake people up in the early morning?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Please make sure they do not come to Mountbatten either.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, the data that the Member has provided are probably accurate.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The bigger, noisier airplanes are only limited mostly to the day time and up to 10 o'clock at night.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Post-10.00 pm, sometimes, it will be for medical evacuation and smaller aircraft.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We take the point that aircraft do bring noise into, not just Nee Soon South, but to other areas of Singapore because of the small land mass of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, CAAS will continue to adopt the best practices according to international standards to include the best practices in noise abatement measures.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: If residents can be woken up at 3.00 am, 4.00 am, I think the noise is not little.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, I would seriously want to urge the Minister and CAAS to look into this issue so that the residents' sleep does not have to be disturbed so often.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Yes, I thank the hon Member for the feedback.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Some of these inconveniences will definitely be reviewed consistently to make sure that we bring the least disamenities to residents.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: These noise abatement measures, from my memory, do take into account school examinations, for instance, when there will be curtailing of flying.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And for the military aircraft, if my memory serves me right, they try to land by 10.00 pm, unless it is for operational contingencies.
